content: ### **List of Contents** Create Delete ### **Objective** Create Reference Line as needed to check its original shape when editing the Pattern. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146407540505)Transform Pattern** ### **Operation** **Create** 1. For instance, solidify creases on the back of the knee area of a pair of jeans to maintain its shape while simulating (ver2.5.0). **Location** 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶**Solidify** **Operation** 1. 3D Toolbar ▶Select a 3D Pattern with ![Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146205100057) **Select/Move** tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ **Solidify** → The selected Pattern is now being solidified. 3. title: Spiral Pattern (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Create a Spiral pattern in a 2D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Spiral** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Spiral.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145732062105) **Spiral** **Operation** 1. After setting the options below, click OK. **Radius** | Set the radius at which a spiral pattern rotates. ---|--- **Length** | Set the length of the inner/outer segment of the spiral pattern. **Side** | Set the inside/outside width of the spiral pattern. **Offset** | Adjust the spacing between spirals. title: Hi/Low-Resolution Garment
content: ### **Objective** Enhance or lower the resolution of Garments. Use this function to enhance the Garment completion in order to emphasize reality and higher quality of a Garment and on the other hand, reduce it for faster adjustments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶**Hi-Res Garment** / **Low-Res Garment** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Hi_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481358233) **Hi-Res Garment** / ![Low_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481367833) **Low-Res Garment** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶**Hi-Res Garment** / **Low-Res Garment** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Hi_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481358233) **Hi-Res Garment** / ![Low_Res Garment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144481367833) **Low-Res Garment** → Hi/Low-Res Properties window appears. 2. Adjust the value for each item. **Garment** | **Particle Distance** | Sets the Particle Distance value applying to all Patterns. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 5mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 20mm ---|---|--- **Tolerance** | Applies only for Patterns within the range of application of Particle Distance. The default tolerance value is between 5mm ~ 20mm, and any Pattern within the range set above is going to be applied. **※ Note:** This is provided to maintain the particle distance value of small patterns below 5mm for more stable simulation. Being mindful of the tolerance can avoid unintentional changes to these patterns. **Add'l Thickness - Collision** | Sets the collision thickness value applying to all patterns. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 1mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 2.5mm **Tolerance** | Any Pattern within the range set above is going to be applied. **Avatar** | **Skin Offset** | Sets the skin offset value applying to avatar. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: 0mm \- Low-Res Garment default value: 3mm **Tolerance** | Any Avatar within the range set above is going to be applied. **Simulation** | **Simulation Quality** | Sets the simulation quality as **Complete** or **Normal**. \- Hi-Res Garment default value: **Complete** \- Low-Res Garment default value: **Normal** **※ Note:** Set the simulation quality on **Complete** for material properties generated in Emulator Mode to result the most accurate simulation. However it may slow down the simulation speed therefore it is recommended to apply this setting when enhancing the garment completion. **Check On/Off Menus** | Toggle option whether to apply on Garment, Avatar, Simulation settings. 3. Click **OK** button. → The adjustments are now being applied. 4. Activate the Simulation. → The adjustments are now being applied to Garment Simulation.
content_description: This page provides guidance on how to enhance or lower the resolution of garments to achieve high-quality visuals or facilitate faster adjustments in 3D simulation.

title: Add Perpendicular Internal Line
content: **List of Contents** Add from a Point Add from a Segment **Objective** Create Internal Lines perpendicular to Pattern outlines or 2D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** **Operation** **Add from a Point** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** 2. Right click on the point of a Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Hover the mouse over the **Add Perpendicular Internal Line** option. → Below options appear. **X-Axis** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's X-axis. ---|--- **Y-Axis** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's Y-axis. **Local** | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on the selected segment. 4. Select the desired option. →The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window with different options appears based on your selection. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- | X-Axis/ Y-Axis | Local (Pattern outline) | Local (Internal Line) Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in Internal Line's length. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the **Length** value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Both (ver5.0.0) | Add Internal Line on both sides of the selected point. Opposite Segment | Not Applicable | Internal Line is created based on the other side of the selected line. Reverse | Not Applicable | The Internal Line is reversed. **Add from a Segment** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144373593625) **Edit Pattern** 2. Right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Add Perpendicular Internal Line**. → The Internal Line preview appears at the center of the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line. → The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. 4. Configure below options as needed and click OK. Option | Description ---|--- Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in the length of the Internal Line. Distance to Segment Edge | Locate the Internal Line. The Internal Line preview shifts as number changes. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the **Length** value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Both (ver5.0.0) | Add Internal Line on both sides of the selected line. Reverse | The Internal Line is reversed. → The Internal Line is created accordingly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for creating internal lines perpendicular to pattern outlines or within a 2D window using the "Edit Pattern" feature in the software.

title: 2D Snapshot (1:1)
content: **Objective** Save real size 2D pattern (1:1). **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Pattern (1:1)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Pattern (1:1)** → 2D window is enlarged, 2D Snapshot window appears. 2. Set below details as needed. 3. Locate the patterns according to the selected setting size (paper), Click **Save**. **Size** | **Preset** | Customize or select from provided preset options. ---|---|--- **Orientation** | Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. **Resolution** | Sets the pixels per inch for the image. **Options** | **Fabric Image** | View or hide the fabric image. **Graphic Image** | View or hide the graphic image. **Reset** | Resets the options back to the program default settings. 4. In order to save the file, enter desired file name and location, then click **Save**. → The image can be saved in .png or .pdf file format. **※ Note:** * Now you can select segments with the ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144211277081) **Edit Pattern** tool and the selected segments will be highlighted in the 2D Snapshot image (ver3.2.0). * Prior to saving the 2D Snapshot image, you can now arrange patterns with the ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144275855641) **Transform Pattern** tool (ver3.2.0). * Save the image background as transparent (ver3.2.0). * Toggle symmetry, instance, trims, and measurements for graphics on or off (ver3.2.0). * 2D snapshots can only be saved as .png format in ver4.0.0 and below.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for saving a real-size 2D pattern snapshot in various formats, allowing users to customize settings such as size, orientation, and resolution.

title: Create Custom Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Open Modular Template Load and Place Patterns Sew Patterns and Block Boxes ## **Objective** Create a Block of a desired Garment and apply it to your design. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Click the Mode button on the right top corner ▶ **MODULAR** ## **Operation** **Open Modular Template** 1. Click the **Modular Template Presets** on the right top corner of Block Editor. → Modular Template Presets window appears. 2. Select a desired Garment category and Modular Template type, click **OK**. → The selected Modular Template appears in the 2D window. **Load and Place Patterns** 1. Add desired Garment files to place into the Block Boxes. 2. Place the Patterns of added Garment to the Blcok Boxes. → The Patterns are linked into the Block Boxes. → The Patterns are automatically arranged to the avatar in 3D Window. (ver 7.0) 3. Sew Patterns to Blcok Boxes, then Simulate. **Sew Patterns and Block Boxes** 1. Click on **![Segment Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144062952089)Segment Sewing** or ![Free Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144082386073) **Free Sewing** tool. 2. Sew Patterns and Block Boxes. **※ Note:** * Patterns that are sewn alone ( i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * When sewing Block Boxes and Blocks, M:N Sewing cannot be used. Only 1:N Sewing can be used for Block Boxes to be 1. * Difference in length between the actual Patterns and the Block Boxes has no effect on the Simulation. * To show Sewing Lines between Block Boxes and Patterns, activate the ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53144062963353)**Show Modular Sewing/Show Pattern Sewing** tool. This tool is activated by default in the Modular Mode. Click it again to either hide or show all Sewing Lines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to create and manipulate garment blocks using modular templates and sewing patterns within the Block Editor interface.

title: Internal Polygon/Line
content: ### **Objective** Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Internal Polygon_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143609271321) **Internal Polygon/Line** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Internal Polygon_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143609271321) **Internal Polygon/Line** 2. Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. 4. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. 5. Use**Length** , **Mirror Creation,** and **Position** options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Length** | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the **Mirror Creation** option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. **Option** **(ver5.0.0)** | Mirror Creating | The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. **Position** | Left | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. 6. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. **※ Note:****** * Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. → An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. → An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. * Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating internal polygons and lines within a pattern using the 2D toolbar in Clo3D.

title: Select/Move Point/Segment
content: **List of Contents** Select Move ### **Objective** Modify Patterns, Internal, and Base (ver5.2) Shapes by moving points and segments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** **Operation** **Select** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012650767/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** 2. Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. → The point or segment is selected. → When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) 3. To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. → All clicked points and segments are selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. → All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. **Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037147)**Transform Pattern** 2. Click and drag the Pattern or use the [arrow keys](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000376767-%EB%B0%A9%ED%96%A5%ED%82%A4%EB%A1%9C-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99). 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. → The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope.→ The center point of the dart is moved along the direction of the center line's tilt **(ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142637530649)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=mOQg7GggSZkBW3dn&t=2557)**)** 4. title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
content: **List of Contents** Import FBX Export FBX **Objective** By Importing an FBX file, Geometry, Material, Joint, Camera, and Camera Animation information are also imported **Operation** **Import FBX / Import (Add) FBX** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import/Import (Add) ▶**FBX** → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Import FBX window appears. 3. Select the settings and click **OK**. → The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Basic | **Load Type** | Open or import the FBX file. ---|---|--- **Object Type** | Import the FBX file as Avatar or Trim. **Scale** | Select the unit or enter the specific value. **Object** | **Camera** | Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported. **Animation** | Toggles whether the Animation data is imported. **Cache** **Animation (MC)** | Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. **Axis Conversion (ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142603909657)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=gL8VgdcciiEKfWLn&t=1538)**)** | Change the direction of each axis of the object. **Option** | **Move Garment to Start Position** | Jump to the position of the start frame of the motion where the garment was loaded and move it.. **※ Note:** Among the avatar skinning types, Dual Quaternion and Eblend are not compatible with CLO. **Export FBX** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶**FBX** → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click**OK**. → The Export OBJ window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click **OK**. → The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. **** **Object** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** | **Select an Avatar** | Select the avatar to be exported. **※ Note:** The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. ---|---|--- **Single/Multiple** | Exports selected objects as Single or Multiple Objects. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360100786234) **Unweld/** **Weld** | When exporting, the connected Vertex(Mesh's points) where seamlines are set in the pattern are combined into individual objects or a single point. ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360102949453) **Weld selected Patterns in Workspace** | Weld the selected patterns connected by sewing lines. **Thin / Thick** | Sets whether to export geometry of the rendering thickness. **Unified UV Coordinates (PNG)** | Exports the texture information of all garment patterns to fit within the UV coordinate values between 0 and 1. Image Scale | Set image scales. Fill Texture Seams | This Function expands the range of the texture based on the border of the texture. **Include Internal Shapes** | The information of the Internal Line included in the garment is also exported. **Option** | **Animation** | When the FBX file is loaded, the animation information in the file is saved together. **Cache Animation (MC)** | Save the recorded garment animation as cache data together. **Basic** | **Scale** | Enter a number or select the desired unit from "Unit of file to be imported" and adjust the scale of the object. **Animation** | Entire Region | Save the recorded garment's animation entirely. Play Region | Only the garment animation in the play area is saved. **File Type** | Select whether to save as Binary / Ascii. * The file is stored in binary and cannot be opened by the user. * Ascii: The file is saved as text so the user can open and understand it. **Texture** | **Relative Texture Image File Path** | Save only the texture name without the texture image path, so if the saved FBX file and the texture image used in the file are in the same path, the texture image is automatically loaded. **Absolute Texture Image File Path** | Save the folder path where the texture image was located as the texture image path. If the path of the texture image is changed, the texture image cannot be loaded. **Embed Media (.zip)** | Export as a zip file along with the texture files used. **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When a color is applied to the texture, it is saved as a combined color and texture. **※ Note:** FBX files cannot contain all data, texture images and color values so select that option to export color information applied to textures as well. **File** | **Save Colorways** | Export the garment with colorways Go back to the List of Contents

title: Edit V-Ray Render Properties
content: ### **Objective** Configure render properties for the final render image. ### **Location** Render Toolbar ▶ ![render_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36781019890457) Render Properties. ### **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Render properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Refer to the below table and edit the settings as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Render Engine** | **Render Engine** | Choose the computer engine to run the render. **CPU** | Run the render with CPU. **GPU (CUDA)** | Run the render with GPU (CUDA). **GPU (OpenCL)** | Run the render with GPU (OpenCL). **CPU Supporting** | Use CPU along with GPU when rendering. Toggle off this option to not use CPU. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as GPU (CUDA). **Low GPU Priority** | Lower GPU priority when rendering. GPU is firstly used in other functions and then used in render. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as either GPU (CUDA) or GPU (OpenCL). **Finish Conditions** | **Noise Threshold** | Set the Noise Threshold for the final render image. The default value is 0.050 and the range is between 0.001 and 0.100. The higher the Noise Threshold is, the more the noise is in the final render image. **Max, Render Time (min)** | The time used for rendering is about two minutes on average when default settings are used for render, light, and image/video properties. However, any modification on the properties may alter the render time. With this option, decide the maximum time that can be used for rendering per image. **Quality** | Adjust the render quality of lights and materials. The Quality can be adjusted to four levels: Low, Medium, High, and Very High. As the option is set towards Very High, render speed decreases. **📝****Note:** * Increase the Quality to render white fur. * Increase the Quality to express light reflections more realistically when textures are added to the studio environment such as the wall and floor. **Light** | Adjust the quality of the light. **Material** | Adjust the quality of materials. **Mesh Optimization** **(Final** **Render Only)** **** **** | **Knitwear** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40170473107609) Optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image. This option only appears when Camera Lens is selected as Default. **Frustum Culling** | No knitwear mesh is created outside the view frustum. A minor difference may appear in the final rendered image when Frustum Culling is enabled. This setting removes all meshes that are out of the camera's view. **LOD** | Level of Detail. The number of knitwear meshes is reduced based on their distance from the camera, with greater distances resulting in fewer meshes. **Color Mapping** | Calibrate the final image color. **Type** **(ver 7.2**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=LlQ6koe3LMps8Meq&t=3057)**)** | Choose the type of Color Mapping. **Reinhard** | The closer the Burn value is to 1.0, the more the image color is multiplied simply by the brightness, and the closer it is to 0.0, the more the color is saturated by the brightness. **HSV exponential****** | Similar to Reinhard's Burn value of 0.0, the ratio of color (RGB) remains. **📝****Note:** * Use the **Open** , **Save** buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting. * To optimize the render speed, please refer to the below directions. 1\. When your OS is Windows: a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **GPU (OpenCL)** for **Engine** for faster render time. 2\. When your OS is Mac:**( ver 2025.0**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c)[**)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c) a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **CPU** for **Engine** for faster render time.
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for configuring render properties to optimize the quality and efficiency of final render images.

title: Edit Texture
content: **List of Contents** Move Zoom In/Out and Rotate Rotate Grainline Setting options **Objective** Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ **Edit Texture** 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ ![_______2D___.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005711127) **Edit Texture** **Operation** **Move** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click ▶ Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. **Zoom In/Out and Rotate** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a pattern with fabric applied. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Click on the diagonal, vertical, horizontal lines of the gizmo ▶ drag, or drag along the gizmo circle. → Diagonal line : The size of the texture image is adjusted while the aspect ratio is maintained. → Horizontal/ Vertical: Texture images are scaled only in the vertical and horizontal directions. → Circle : The texture image is rotated. 4. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Simulate once it is adjusted. → The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. **※ Note:** You can directly enter the angle in the Pattern Properties ▶ Fabric ▶ Grain Direction menu, and if you turn off the Link All Colorways menu, you can apply the different grain direction for each colorway. **Setting options** 1. For symmetrical patterns, the selected segment and symmetric line are matched. **Delete Texture** | Delete the texture. **Flip Texture Horizontally/ Vertically** | Flip the texture horizontally or vertically. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on modifying fabric grainlines, adjusting texture images, and utilizing editing tools for individual patterns in a 2D/3D design environment.

title: Skive
content: ### **Objective** Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ **Skive** **Operation** 1. Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592427/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592407/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern **tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ **Skive** → The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. → A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of one ('1') to one hundred ('100') in **Percentage (%)**. 3. Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. 4. Activate the ![Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024827668/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulate**. → The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.

Click the ![Face.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45583162671257) **Face tab** at the top. **_**✨Tip:**_** When switching to the Face tab after compositing the background first, the result is automatically applied as the Target Image. This allows you to swap the face while keeping the background result. 2. Generate a face image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select gender, age, and ethnicity, and enter your prompt. **✨ Writing Tips:** * **List the words. ** Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. * **Emphasize certain words more. ** If parentheses are used around a word you want to emphasize, it carries more weight. Weight increase rate: (word) 1.1 times, ((word)) 1.21 times. ![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33834084288537)**Maintain Prompt** | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Face image is created anew each time. Click the Upload button next to Target Image to load the render image to be composited. For more accurate analysis and results, it is recommended to use an image that fits the following guidelines: ▪️ High-resolution image (2160 to 4320 pixels recommended) ▪️ Well-focused and sharp image ▪️ Image with good contrast between objects and background. ▪️ Consistent lighting ▪️ Appropriately sized image 2.
